statements.t: In September 2026, we announced a plan to restructure the Company to prioritize development of our in vivo -engineered TCR-T therapy candidates for the treatment of patients with solid tumors (the “2026 Reorganization”).
As part of this strategic realignment, we implemented a workforce reduction of approximately 75%, which is expected to produce cumulative cost savings of $55.0 million through the end of 2027.
In connection with the workforce reduction, we expect to incur approximately $4.4 million in employee-related costs, consisting primarily of pay continuation and related benefits.
We expect to complete the 2026 Reorganization and incur virtually all charges by the end of the fourth quarter of 2027.

To advance our solid tumor program, we are developing in vivo -engineered TCR-T therapy candidates that target cancer-specific antigens expressed in various solid tumor indications, including melanoma, ovarian cancer, non-small cell lung cancer, and head and neck cancer.

We believe that an in vivo engineering approach will overcome the key limitations of ex vivo -engineered autologous TCR-T, including the cost and difficulty of patient-specific manufacturing, the delay in getting product to patients, and the need for lymphodepletion.
As with our ex vivo program, we will initially treat patients with single TCR-T candidates (singleplexed therapy).
We expect this to be sufficient for cancers with uniform target expression.
Our first two therapeutic candidates, one targeting PRAME and the other targeting MAGE-A4, are advancing through IND-enabling studies.
We expect to share preclinical data in Q1 2027 and file our first IND in Q3 2027, with plans to dose our first patient in Q4 2027.
We remain committed to the care of patients and intend to continue collecting safety and efficacy data while actively exploring strategic partnerships that could continue to move the program forward.
While primarily focused on oncology, we believe our target discovery platform is well suited to identify targets that cause T cell-driven autoimmune disorders.
We have previously identified the targets of pathogenic T-cells in HLA-B*27 associated autoimmune disorders, including ankylosing spondylitis.

Since our inception in 2018, we have devoted our efforts to raising capital, obtaining financing, filing, prosecuting and maintaining intellectual property rights, organizing and staffing our Company and incurring research and development (“R&D”) costs related to the identification of novel targets for TCRs and development of TCR-T therapy product candidates to target and eliminate cancer cells.

We will not generate revenue from sales of our therapies unless and until we successfully complete clinical development and obtain regulatory approval for one or more of our product candidates.

If we obtain regulatory approval for any of our product candidates, we expect to incur significant expenses related to developing our commercialization capability to support the sales, marketing and distribution of those therapies.
As a result, we will need substantial additional funding to support our continuing operations and pursue our growth strategy.

Until such time as we can generate significant revenue from sales of our therapies, if ever, we expect to finance our operations through a combination of equity offerings, debt financings, or other capital sources, including collaborations with other companies, and other strategic transactions.

Because of the numerous risks and uncertainties associated with TCR-T therapy product candidate development, we are unable to accurately predict the timing or amount of increased expenses or when, or if, we will be able to achieve or maintain profitability.
We have based this estimate on assumptions that may prove to be wrong, and we could exhaust our available capital resources sooner than we expect.
The Notice has no effect on the listing of our common stock at this time, and our common stock will continue to trade on The Nasdaq Global Market under the symbol “TCRX.”

If the Staff concludes we will not be able to cure the deficiency, or if we do not regain compliance, the Staff will provide written notification to us indicating our common stock will be subject to delisting.

We will continue to monitor the bid price of our common stock and consider our available options to regain compliance with the Minimum Bid Price Rule, but there can be no assurance we will be able to regain compliance.
On August 12, 2026, we received notice from Amgen of its election to terminate the agreement which will be effective November 10, 2026.
We have based our current operating plan on assumptions that may prove to be wrong, and we could utilize our available capital resources sooner than we expect.

Until such time, if ever, as we can generate substantial product revenue, we expect to finance our operations through a combination of equity offerings, debt financings, collaborations, strategic alliances and marketing, distribution or licensing arrangements.

To the extent that we raise additional capital through the sale of equity or convertible debt securities, your ownership interest will be diluted, and the terms of these securities may include liquidation or other preferences that adversely affect your rights as a common stockholder.
We have not yet received regulatory approval for or commercialized any of our product candidates and do not expect to generate revenue from product sales for several years, if at all.

We do not expect to generate any product revenue unless and until we (i) complete development of any of our product candidates; (ii) obtain applicable regulatory approvals; and (iii) successfully commercialize or enter into collaborative agreements for our product candidates.
We expect to incur continuing significant losses for the foreseeable future.
We will require additional capital to develop our product candidates and fund our operations into the foreseeable future.

Furthermore, our operating plans may change in the future, and we will continue to require additional capital to meet operational needs and capital requirements associated with such operating plans.
However, as we continue to evolve as a business, we will incur increased costs related to legal and financial compliance.
Our status as an emerging growth company will end on December 31, 2026, which will be the last day of the fiscal year ending after the fifth anniversary of our initial public offering.
